subject: [RFC PATCH 4/4] mm/zswap: move reclaim-driven writeback to a kworker

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the deferred writeback workers hold a reference to the memcg, and requested that queued workers be stopped before calling try_to_unmap() to prevent lock ordering violations.

Reviewer noted that the current implementation may not scale as the number of workers increases, requesting further testing and discussion.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti noted that the writeback bio is issued as root, incurring debt to the cgroup, and with this series throttling the bio at submission, reclaimers would stall on a single cgroup's IO budget; he suggested deferring writeback for everyone.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti noted that the shrinker's behavior needs discussion to prevent zswap from draining 'hot' pages, and suggested clarifying the justifications for all behavioral changes in the next version.

Reviewer noted that while the deferred writeback workers hold a reference to the memcg, they do not drop theirs when they finish, potentially causing issues with reclaim paths.

Reviewer noted that kworker may stall due to exhausting the memcg's IO budget, potentially starving other memcgs, and suggested this as a valid reason for moving writeback to a kworker.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Nhat,

On Tue, Sep 29, 2026 at 3:43 PM Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com> wrote:

---

It would not scale indeed, the worker does not accumulate in this
version of the patch. That needs to be tested and discussed.

---

Today the writeback bio is issued as root, which incurs debt to the
cgroup. The submitting task repays it on return to user or on any
other IO of the cgroup until the debt is paid off.

With this series the bio is throttled at submission instead, so
whoever submits it sleeps until the cgroup has budget:
- for direct reclaimers, that's the application latency we observed
- for kswapd reclaim, it would stall on a single cgroup's IO budget

So we need to defer for everyone.

---

In the large production workload I have worked on, when the shrinker
is enabled, the zswap pool size decreases by ~97%. So I did not want
to accumulate "too much" work to prevent zswap from draining "hot"
pages, it acts like an additional throttling mechanism. But that needs
discussion, hence the RFC.

And you're right, In the next version, I'll clearly point out all the
behavioral changes I made with their justifications.

---

Yes, this is another behavioural change that I will explain in the next version.

Indeed the work piles up in the shrinker control loop if writeback
cannot catch up but note that it is bounded, which is what we want
right?

---

You're right, and the explanation is "we cannot starve other memcgs if
one worker stalls because it exhausted its memcg budget".

Thanks Nhat!

Alex

2026-09-30.patch_summary: This patch moves the reclaim-driven writeback of zswap to a kworker, which writes back data in chunks of SWAP_CLUSTER_MAX entries at a time while holding a reference on the memcg. This change is made to prevent stalls caused by uninterruptible sleeps when the owning cgroup's IO budget is exceeded. The shrinker now reports nothing freed until the worker has run and completed the writeback.
